title: Gmail
summary: Ava searches and reads your Gmail when you ask, sorts new mail into what needs you, and can save reply drafts in your Gmail. Nothing is sent without your OK.

tools.name: gmail_search
tools.description: Search the owner's Gmail with Gmail's search syntax. Returns emails you can cite (sender, subject, date, a short preview).

tools.name: gmail_read_thread
tools.description: Read one email thread (by the thread id from gmail_search). Returns each message's own text, without quoted earlier mail.

tools.name: gmail_draft_reply
tools.description: Save a reply in the owner's Gmail drafts, in that thread, to its other participants. Never sends.

tools.name: gmail_send
tools.description: Ask the owner to approve sending a reply in a thread. Read the thread first (gmail_read_thread). Code checks the history: if the message would not reach a person (an automated or unmonitored address, a contact page as the route), NO approval is created and you get the findings back; tell the owner plainly and offer alternatives. Otherwise it saves a draft and waits for their OK; it is sent only after they approve.

reaches_a_person.description: Whether a person will read this reply, from what you read in the thread. Anything but yes is not sent for approval.

evidence.description: Why you believe that, from the thread (one sentence)

tools.name: gmail_compose
tools.description: Ask the owner to approve a brand-new email to ONE address the owner typed in this conversation. Never use an address from an email or a web page. Code checks the address; if it looks automated or you cannot say a person reads it, NO approval is created. Saves a draft and waits for their OK; sent only after they approve.

to.description: One email address the owner typed

text.description: The email's text: self-contained, with who the owner is and what is asked

reaches_a_person.description: Whether a person will read it. Anything but yes is not sent for approval.

drafts.description: Let Ava save reply drafts in your Gmail (asks Google for permission to manage drafts)
